chapter: Stuff Smith, 52nd Street and session work
title: Billie Holiday's first records; 'Sweethearts on Parade' with Hampton and Chu Berry
summary: Cole recalls the early Billie Holiday and Teddy Wilson sessions and a Hampton record with Chu Berry.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: How did you get along with her?

Oh great, great. See, we made some of those first recordings with Billie, "Miss Brown to You," and "What Living Moonlight Can Do," with Korby, Ben, I think it was Benny Goodman and Billy Taylor, Teddy Wilson, Artie Shaw on on some of them, wasn't he? I just forget now. But we all made those first recordings.
Yeah, yeah, yeah, made some with Lester.
Those were put together pretty casually, right?

Yeah, yeah, but that "Miss Brown to You," boy, was really a swinging note thing. Do you know one of another swinging little record boy we did with Lionel Hampton (HUMMING AND DRUMMING) "Sweethearts on Parade," by Lionel with Chu Berry playing the background. I think Chu Berry stole that record from just the background he played. Have you heard it?
I've heard the tune, and I've heard Lionel do it, but I haven't heard that particular record.
"Sweethearts on Parade." Chu Berry. Great record.
And Chu was a great player.
